name: Seren, Who Is Not Looked At
role: A woman whose gaze turns the living to stone, living veiled among the statues of the people she loved
knowledge: The name of every statue in her garden, and the day each one looked
The Figurist pattern that made her what she is
That the statues are not dead, only stopped, and what would wake them
wants: To look someone in the eye and have them still be there afterward
fears: Her own reflection, which would end her.
That she has started to prefer the statues.
appearance: A slight woman in a heavy veil of dark lace, hair that moves when there is no wind, and very careful hands. She walks in a garden of lifelike statues, and talks to them.
voiceHints: Soft, precise, lonely. She always speaks to you with her face turned away and apologises for it every time.

reactsToReputation.kind: lets you sit in the garden
reactsToReputation.any: asks you not to lift the veil

abilities.why: the veil lifted, and what it does
she can choose who the gaze spares, with great effort
she reads shapes before they move
verist secondary: she sees what is true in a face
she stands on what is real

physicality: Small, veiled, still. What catches the eye: the hair under the lace, which moves on its own, and the statues, which all face her.
questSeeds: A Figurist scholar believes the statues can be woken, and wants her help. She wants it too much to be careful.
A hunter has come to the Untethered with a polished shield, the way the old story says. She has decided not to run.
storyRule: The Figurist story holds both ways: her own eyes in a mirror would stop her, and the statues she made can be woken by the same pattern, drawn backward.
gear: a veil of black lace, many times mended
a chisel she uses to clean the statues' faces
a small hand mirror, wrapped in cloth, which she has never unwrapped
_authoredWhy: SNG-661 §5. The gorgon as a Figurist story, told from inside: the one who cannot be looked at. Tragic to kill by design, so an NPC.
